lazyload.description: DEPRECATED location. Lazy-load settings now live at DotSee:ResponsiveImages:LazyLoad. This root-level section is still honoured for existing sites, but the nested one wins if both are present.

useWebP.description: DEPRECATED location. Use DotSee:ResponsiveImages:UseWebP instead. This root-level key is still honoured for existing sites, but the nested one wins if both are present.

ResponsiveImages.description: Responsive image settings: rule sets, lazy loading, WebP and which backend generates the URLs.

RuleSets.description: The named rule sets you reference from views via rule-set="...".

UseWebP.description: Append &format=webp to every generated image URL. Requires an image processor that supports WebP output. Leave this off if a CDN in front of the site already negotiates image formats (Cloudflare Polish, format=auto and similar).

SuppressTagHelperWarnings.description: Stop the tag helpers rendering their red warning messages into the page when an image is misconfigured (missing alt text, missing rule set, render error). Leave false in development so problems are visible; set true in production via an environment-specific appsettings file. Errors are logged either way.

UrlProvider.description: Which backend generates image URLs. "Umbraco" (the default) emits image-processor query strings resolved by the origin. "Cloudflare" emits /cdn-cgi/image/... URLs so the resizing happens at the edge instead, which requires transformations to be enabled on the zone serving the site. Everything else - rule sets, breakpoints, focal point, art direction, LQIP, markup - behaves identically either way.

CloudflareImageSettings.description: Options for the Cloudflare URL provider. Only read when UrlProvider is "Cloudflare". Every value has a working default, so this section can be omitted entirely.

Prefix.description: Path prefix Cloudflare listens on for transformations. Change it only if the site serves transformations through a Worker route rather than the built-in endpoint.

BaseUrl.description: Absolute origin to prefix generated URLs with, e.g. https://images.example.com. Leave unset to emit relative URLs, which is correct when the site itself is the Cloudflare zone doing the transforming.

Format.description: Cloudflare format option. "auto" serves AVIF or WebP by content negotiation, which is the one thing a CDN does better than this package. Use "none" or an empty string to keep the source format. Overridden per call when UseWebP is on, which forces webp.

Metadata.description: Cloudflare metadata option. "none" strips EXIF entirely, "copyright" keeps only the copyright tag, "keep" preserves everything. Unset by default, which leaves Cloudflare's own behaviour (keep the copyright tag, drop the rest) in place and keeps the option out of the URL.

CacheBuster.description: Append the media item's cache buster to the source URL, as Umbraco's own crop URLs do, so replacing a media file in place produces new URLs at the edge rather than serving the old image until its TTL expires. Turn off only if media is never replaced in place and the extra billable transformations per edit matter.

OnError.description: Cloudflare onerror option. "redirect" serves the untransformed original when a transformation fails, so an unsupported source degrades to a working image rather than a broken one. Empty omits the option.

LegacyRuleSetArray.description: DEPRECATED layout. DotSee:ResponsiveImages used to be the rule set array itself. Still honoured for existing sites; prefer moving the array under a "RuleSets" key so lazy-load and WebP settings can sit alongside it.

RuleSet.description: A named set of breakpoints and options, referenced from views by name.

Name.description: Unique identifier for this rule set. Referenced in views as rule-set="hero".

Breakpoints.description: The viewport thresholds this rule set switches image sizes at.

Sizes.description: Entries for the CSS sizes attribute, describing how wide the image is laid out at each viewport, e.g. "(max-width: 576px) 100vw" then "50vw". Used by <ds:img>; <ds:picture> uses media queries instead. A trailing default equal to the widest generated image is appended automatically. Omitting this makes the browser assume the image fills that width at every viewport and download more than it needs on small screens.

OriginalImageMaxWidth.description: Ceiling for generated image widths, and the width used for the fallback src. Not a display size: width/height attributes are derived from the largest breakpoint, not from this.

OriginalImageMaxHeight.description: Ceiling for generated image heights. Setting both maximums lets width/height attributes be emitted from configuration alone, without depending on each media item's umbracoWidth/umbracoHeight.

ImageQuality.description: JPEG/WebP quality, 1-100. When unset (0), no quality option is added to generated URLs and the image processor's own default applies.

Use2x.description: Also generate a 2x (retina) variant. In it becomes an extra 2x candidate on the same ; in it becomes an extra, wider w candidate.

CropMode.description: How the image is fitted to the requested dimensions. Defaults to Crop (the first value of Umbraco's ImageCropMode enum) when unset.

UseBreakPointWidthIfNoWidth.description: When a breakpoint sets no Width, generate the image at the breakpoint's own width instead of deriving it from the height.

LazyLoad.description: Overrides the global LazyLoad.EnablelazyLoad setting for this rule set. Leave null to inherit. A null global means lazy loading is off regardless.

UseFocalPoint.description: Anchor generated crops on the focal point the editor set in the backoffice rather than the image centre. Set false for plain centre cropping.

RuleBreakPoint.description: One viewport threshold and the image size to generate for it.

BreakPointWidth.description: Viewport width threshold in pixels, used in the min-width media query. A threshold, not a display width - the image generated here is set by Width.

Width.description: Pixel width of the image to generate at this breakpoint. If 0, falls back to BreakPointWidth when UseBreakPointWidthIfNoWidth is true.

Height.description: Pixel height of the image to generate. Set 0 to resize by width only and keep the source aspect ratio.

LazyLoadSettings.description: Global lazy-loading settings. Individual rule sets can override with their own LazyLoad property.

EnablelazyLoad.description: Enable native loading="lazy" globally. Null disables lazy loading regardless of any rule set's own setting.

PreviewType.description: Which placeholder to show while a lazy image loads. Blur inlines a tiny base64 copy of the image itself, costing no extra request. LowResImage shows one shared placeholder file. Omit for no placeholder.

LowResImagePath.description: Path to a generic placeholder image. Only used when PreviewType is LowResImage.

ImageCdnSettings.description: Optional CDN purging, so replaced media stops being served from the edge. Everything here is off unless explicitly enabled.

Enabled.description: Master switch. While false no CDN call of any kind is made and the rest of this section is ignored.

Provider.description: Which CDN to talk to. Any unrecognised value disables purging.

ZoneId.description: Cloudflare zone id for the zone serving the site. Purging is skipped if missing.

ApiToken.description: API token with the Zone / Cache Purge permission. Keep this out of appsettings.json - use user secrets or an environment variable (DotSee__ImageCdn__ApiToken).

BaseUrl.description: Public origin of the site, e.g. https://www.example.com. Required for Files mode, which needs absolute URLs.

PurgeOnMediaSave.description: Purge when a media item is saved. Still gated by Enabled.

PurgeOnMediaDelete.description: Purge when a media item is deleted. Still gated by Enabled.

Mode.description: Files purges the changed media's own URL and the variant URLs the rule sets ask for - targeted, but best effort. Everything purges the whole zone on every qualifying change: reliable and very blunt, since it discards the cache for the entire site.

MaxUrlsPerPurge.description: Upper bound on URLs submitted per media change, so a rule set with many breakpoints cannot produce an unbounded request.
